title: An associated prime stays associated after localizing at it (any ring)
statement: Let $T$ be a commutative ring, $P$ a $T$-module and $\mathfrak q\subset T$ a prime ideal. For a commutative ring $T$ and a $T$-module $P$ call a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$ an *associated prime* of $P$ if $\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)=\{a\in T:az=0\}$ for some $z\in P$, and write $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ for the set of them. Let $T_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localization of $T$ at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qT_{\mathfrak q}$, and $P_{\mathfrak q}$ the localization of $P$ at $T\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], a $T_{\mathfrak q}$-module. If $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$, then $\mathfrak qT_{\mathfrak q}\in\operatorname{Ass}_{T_{\mathfrak q}}(P_{\mathfrak q})$; more precisely, if $\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)=\mathfrak q$ then $\operatorname{Ann}_{T_{\mathfrak q}}(z/1)=\mathfrak qT_{\mathfrak q}$. No Noetherian hypothesis is made.

proof.text: Fix z with Ann_T(z) = q and let J be the annihilator of z/1 in P_q. A scalar a belongs to the contraction of J exactly when a(z/1) = 0. By linearity of the localization map and the zero-fraction criterion (LocalizedModule.mem_ker_mkLinearMap_iff), this is equivalent to the existence of t outside q with t(az) = 0. Thus ta belongs to q; primality and t outside q imply a belongs to q. Conversely, if a belongs to q, az = 0 and t = 1 witnesses localized vanishing. Therefore J.under T = q.

proof.text: The localization ideal correspondence IsLocalization.map_under says that extending the contraction of any ideal J in T_q returns J. Apply it to the annihilator from the first step and substitute J.under T = q. This gives Ann_{T_q}(z/1) = q.map(algebraMap T T_q) for every z with Ann_T(z) = q.

The annihilator equality from the preceding step makes z/1 a witness for association. Combine this with the equality for every witness to obtain both conjuncts.
